entries.name: Debuggable
entries.description: Whether the application can be debugged, even when running on a device in user mode. This is a potential security risk but it also seems to be the only way for Android 12+ to get `adb backup` to include app data.

entries.name: Test Only
entries.description: Indicates whether this application is only for testing purposes. For example, it might expose functionality or data outside of itself that can cause a security hole, but be useful for testing. This kind of APK only installs through `adb`.

entries.name: Uses Cleartext Traffic
entries.description: Indicates whether the app intends to use cleartext network traffic, such as cleartext HTTP. The key reason for avoiding cleartext traffic is the lack of confidentiality, authenticity, and protections against tampering. A network attacker can eavesdrop on transmitted data and also modify it without being detected.

entries.name: Accessibility Service
entries.description: Grants access to a lot of features of the system which are usually unavailable to normal apps to be able to aid users in using their device. However, access to these features can also be abused.

entries.name: Input Method Service
entries.description: Grant the ability to act as IME (Input Method) to enter data. Only apps actually providing input should implement this, otherwise it might be used to capture user input.

entries.name: VPN Service
entries.description: Grants the ability to intercept network traffic. Only VPN and certain privacy-protecting applications, such as non-root ad-blockers/firewalls, should implement this.
